**Created file:** `E:/Hackathon/buddy-agent/app/items.py` ### 📦 What’s inside | Section | Details | |---------|---------| | **Imports** | `APIRouter`, `status` from FastAPI; `List`, `Optional` from typing; `BaseModel`, `Field` from Pydantic | | **Router** | `router = APIRouter()` – ready to be included in the main FastAPI app (`app.include_router(router)`) | | **In‑memory store** | `items_db: List[Item] = []` – a simple list that holds the submitted items for the life of the process | | **Pydantic model** | `Item` with fields:
`id: int`
`name: str`
`description: Optional[str] = None`
All fields have helpful docstrings and `Field` metadata | | **POST endpoint** | `POST /items`
• Accepts a JSON body matching `Item`
• Appends the received item to `items_db`
• Returns the stored item
• Responds with HTTP **201 Created**
• Tagged with `"items"` for OpenAPI grouping | ### 🚀 How to use ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from app.items import router as items_router app = FastAPI() app.include_router(items_router) ``` Now you can POST an item: ```bash curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/items" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"id": 1, "name": "Sample", "description": "A test item"}' ``` Response (201): ```json { "id": 1, "name": "Sample", "description": "A test item" } ``` All requirements are satisfied – a ready‑to‑run FastAPI endpoint with a fully‑typed Pydantic v2 model and mock in‑memory storage.
